layers.name: Integration & OT/IT fabric
layers.purpose: Connect every IT and OT system so agents can read trusted signals and take catalogued, reversible actions in IT systems — while OT data crosses security zones one way.
components: Event streaming and CDC from CIS, MDMS, OMS and EAM
OT data diode / broker for SCADA, EMS and historian (one way)
Green Button for customer data sharing
Tool endpoints for agents (IT systems only)
layers.specifics: CIS, MDMS, AMI head-end, OMS, ADMS/DERMS, EMS, SCADA, historian, GIS, EAM, mobile workforce and ISO/RTO market interfaces; OT data crosses security zones one way through data diodes or brokers; CIM message patterns; Green Button for customer data sharing.
takes: Governed capability catalog of agent tools — none of them in OT zones

failure.text: Without one-way OT flows, analytics either lack grid signals or put OT zones at risk.

layers.governed: Every tool an agent can call is catalogued with its owner, autonomy ceiling and rollback; no tool reaches an OT control device.

layers.name: Data platform (incl. semantic & network model)
layers.purpose: Turn raw utility data into certified data products, one definition per KPI and a governed network model that every agent shares.
components: Bronze → Silver → Gold on open tables
Network connectivity model as a governed data product
IEEE 1366 reliability calculations with major-event-day flags
Semantic views, glossary, CDE register, context layer
layers.specifics: Medallion layers on open tables; network connectivity model as a governed data product; AMI interval data at 15-minute grain; historian time series; IEEE 1366 reliability calculations with major-event-day flags; semantic views for reliability, cost per customer and bad debt.
takes: DQ rules on critical data elements
One certified definition per KPI (e.g. SAIDI with and without MED)

failure.text: Three SAIDI definitions give three answers to the same question.

layers.governed: Classification (PII, CEUD, CEII, Market-Sensitive) is applied at ingestion and enforced by row and column policies in every product.

layers.name: AI / ML foundation
layers.purpose: Give every agent governed models, retrieval, evaluation and a runtime that enforces autonomy levels — including the OT cap.
components: Agent runtime with the OT cap
layers.specifics: Forecasting (load, renewables, outages), computer vision (drone, LiDAR, thermal), asset-health models, retrieval over standards and procedures, and an agent runtime with the OT cap.

failure.text: An unevaluated model drifts and an agent keeps its autonomy.

layers.governed: The runtime refuses any promotion of an OT-capped agent above L2 and logs the attempt.

layers.name: Trust & governance
layers.purpose: Make every answer and action explainable, consented, approved where needed and reversible.
components: Policy enforcement, masking and row access
layers.specifics: Customer energy usage data consent and sharing rules; disconnection protections; rate-case evidence lineage; model risk tiers; human approval for every OT-adjacent recommendation.
takes: Consent propagation for customer energy usage data
Approval matrix per agent and action

failure.text: Customer names reach an operations role that only needs counts.

layers.governed: Approvals, refusals and overrides are written to the Agent Evidence Trail (UDP-AGT-01).

layers.name: Security, privacy & critical-infrastructure protection
layers.purpose: Protect critical infrastructure information and customer data, with least-privilege agent identities and evidence for every standard.
components: Classification and handling of CEII and BES Cyber System Information
No agent credentials in OT zones
Evidence for reliability and cyber standards
layers.specifics: Classification and handling of CEII and BES Cyber System Information; least-privilege agent identities; no agent credentials in OT zones; evidence for reliability and cyber standards.

failure.text: A CEII extract reaches an uncleared role.

layers.governed: CEII access always needs owner approval; agents never hold credentials inside OT security zones.

controlPlane.name: Govern, secure and assure with AI
controlPlane.summary: One control plane across every layer: policy, guardrails, evaluation, approvals, evidence, kill switches — and the OT safety rule.

perLayer.integration: Tool catalog with owners, autonomy ceilings and rollback; no tools in OT zones
perLayer.data: Classification at ingestion; row and column policies; certification gates
perLayer.ai: Evaluation suites, promotion and demotion, the OT cap enforced in the runtime
perLayer.trust: Approval matrix, consent propagation, disconnection protections, audit trail
perLayer.security: Least-privilege agent identities, CEII handling, critical-infrastructure evidence

layers.name: Bronze
layers.text: Raw CIS, MDMS, OMS, GIS, EAM, historian and document landings, append-only

layers.name: Silver
layers.text: Cleansed and conformed to the CIM-aligned utility model; duplicates and estimated reads flagged

layers.name: Gold
layers.text: Outage events with MED flags, customer-to-device links, asset health

layers.name: Glossary
layers.text: SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI (IEEE 1366), major event day, medical baseline, ETR

layers.name: Context
layers.text: Operating rules: OP-07 switching checks, CM-02 ETR source, WF-05 PSPS decisions

layers.name: Data products
layers.text: 31 governed products, from Customer 360 to the Network Connectivity Model

layers.name: Agents
layers.text: 36 flagship agents, OT-facing ones capped at L2

layers.name: Governance rail
layers.text: Policies, approvals, evidence and kill switches across every layer
